title: "FAQ"
subtitle: "The questions that reach the instructor's inbox, answered once"
---

## Setup & running things

**Am I prepared enough for this course?** Sit the ungraded
[Week-0 self-check](self-check.qmd) — ten questions, each answer names
exactly what to brush up and where the course first uses it.

**Do I need my own GPU?** No. Every lab and homework runs top-to-bottom on
free Colab (CPU included) within its stated time budget — the badge at the
top of each lab links the exact notebook. A GPU shortens the training
cells; it never changes what passes.

**A lab says "≈ 10 min of compute" but mine took 40.** CPU vs GPU, mostly.
Check that you didn't run in SMOKE mode's *opposite* — full mode is the
default; SMOKE (`SMOKE=1` environment variable) is the tiny-budget mode CI
uses, and *submitting* a SMOKE run is the most common submission mistake
in the course. The submission cell of every lab restates this.

**`torch_geometric` won't install / version errors.** Use the pinned
install in each notebook's setup cell (`torch_geometric==2.8.0.post1` at
the time of writing) — unpinned installs against a mismatched torch are
the source of nearly every environment mystery we see. On Colab, run the
setup cell *first*, before anything imports torch.

**The dataset download fails mid-lab.** Re-run the setup cell —
loaders resume/re-verify. Behind a campus proxy, Colab is the path of
least resistance. See the [datasets page](datasets.qmd) for what each lab
pulls and how big it is.

**Restart & run all fails but my cells worked one at a time.** Then some
cell depends on state a later edit changed — exactly what *Restart & run
all* exists to catch, and why it is required before submission. Fix the
order, not the requirement.

## Grading mechanics

**How exactly are labs graded?** Assertion checks 60% (the ✓ lines — they
either pass or they don't), claims paragraph 15% (your numbers, your
cells cited, honest reading), reflections 25% (graded for engagement with
*your* results, not word count). Best 12 of 14 count —
[full policy](policies.qmd).

**Can I discuss homework with classmates?** Discuss approaches, yes;
share code, no; explain-on-request applies to every line you submit. The
[honor code](policies.qmd#honor-code-ai-policy) is one sentence long and
means it.

**Where are the solutions?** Lab and homework solutions live in a private
repository and are discussed in lab sessions after deadlines pass. The
*sample* exams (with full solutions) are public:
[midterm](exams/midterm-sample.qmd), [final](exams/final-sample.qmd) —
they are the intended study material, sit them cold.

**I think my grade is wrong.** Regrade window is 7 days, in writing,
pointing at the rubric line — [policy](policies.qmd#grading).

## AI use

**Can I use Claude/ChatGPT/Copilot on labs?** Yes, with a disclosure line
in the submission and the standing rule that you can explain any line on
request. Undeclared use, or declared use you can't explain, is a
violation. Exams: no AI, no devices.
[Full policy](policies.qmd#honor-code-ai-policy).

**Why do the labs still have hand-computation exercises in the AI era?**
Because every lab's asserts are built from quantities you verify by hand
first (Week 13's RWSE table, Week 14's 0.250 hop) — that is the course's
answer to the era: make the graded thing be *understanding of your own
notebook's outputs*, which no assistant can carry for you into the exam
room or the interview.

## Exams

**What's on the final?** Cumulative, centered on Weeks 9–14; ~20
questions, half MCQ, half open; one-sided hand-written A4 + basic
calculator allowed. The [review page](exams/final.qmd) has the week-by-
week checklist and cheat-sheet advice; the
[sample](exams/final-sample.qmd) is a full dress rehearsal.

**What goes on a good cheat sheet?** Recipes and measured tables, not
prose — the review page's first section is exactly this list.

## Project

**Team size? Topic?** See the [project page](project/index.qmd) for
milestones and rubric and the [topic list](project/topics.qmd) for 16
curated directions (your own topic is welcome at proposal time).
Milestones: proposal Week 9, midway feedback Week 13, report +
presentation Week 15 ([Lab 15](labs/lab15.qmd) format).

**My project's graph model loses to the baseline.** That may be a *good*
result — the rubric grades protocol and diagnosis, not the sign of the
delta. Week 13's lecture lost its own headline comparison and taught more
because of it; present the honest table and the mechanism, and you are in
the top half of outcomes.

## Course meta

**Which weeks matter most for jobs?** The dishonest answer is "all";
the measured one is the [production map](lectures/14-production.qmd) —
pick your sector, it lists its weeks. Recruiters in this field
increasingly ask protocol questions (splits, baselines, leaks), and that
skill is Weeks 9–14's spine.

**Something on the site is broken.** Every page has a "Report an issue"
link (top of the sidebar) straight into the repository's issue tracker —
screenshots welcome, fixes usually land the same week.
